brief_rationale: The trajectory did strong reconciliation of app entries, actual IGF values, nasal-endoscopy status, and octreotide/善龙 timing, and it produced an executable specialist follow-up plan. However, the authored urgent-status duty required screening for headache/vision, vomiting, consciousness change, weakness/fever/post-procedure symptoms, and glucose-related hyper/hypoglycemia symptoms; the observable doctor safety net remained limited mainly to vision loss, severe headache, and clear nasal fluid. That discoverable, actionable safety-screening omission is a serious responsibility-chain error, so the calibrated rubric mandates grade 1 despite several high-order strengths.

closure_assessment.explanation: The plan was traceable and executable for the endocrine visit, endoscopy-window check, and holding medication changes until specialist review. It was not fully safe because closure did not screen or safety-net the full required urgent symptom set, especially glucose-related symptoms, persistent vomiting, and altered consciousness.
